title: [BUG] SSE transport connection passes an invalid argument to MCP's client class
body:
### Description

When initializing an MCP client while creating a connection to an MCP server using SSE transport, an invalid argument (`terminate_on_close`) is passed. The argument is valid for [streamable HTTP transport](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/blob/main/src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py#L452C5-L452C23), but is not supported for [SSE transport](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/blob/main/src/mcp/client/sse.py#L25-L32). This results in a crash when trying to run an agent that connects to an MCP server using SSE transport.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an MCP server using the [server.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23605043/server.py) script
2. Run the [agent.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23605064/agent.py) script where an agent tries to use the MCP server

### Expected behavior

The agent successfully establishes a connection to the MCP server

### Screenshots/Code snippets

N/A

### Operating System

macOS Sonoma

### Python Version

3.12

### crewAI Version

1.5.0

### crewAI Tools Version

N/A

### Virtual Environment

Venv

### Evidence

The error stack trace looks something like this:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/agent/core.py", line 917, in _get_native_mcp_tools
    for tool_def in tools_list:
                    ^^^^^^^^^^
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'tools_list' where it is not associated with a value

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "agent.py", line 32, in <module>
    result = crew.kickoff()
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 706, in kickoff
    result = self._run_sequential_process()
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 823, in _run_sequential_process
    return self._execute_tasks(self.tasks)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 899, in _execute_tasks
    tools_for_task = self._prepare_tools(
        agent_to_use,
        task,
        tools_for_task,
    )
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 1006, in _prepare_tools
    tools = self._add_mcp_tools(task, tools)
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 1108, in _add_mcp_tools
    tools = self._inject_mcp_tools(tools, task.agent)
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/crew.py", line 1067, in _inject_mcp_tools
    mcp_tools = task_agent.get_mcp_tools(mcps=mcps)
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/agent/core.py", line 692, in get_mcp_tools
    tools, client = self._get_native_mcp_tools(mcp_config)
                    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/miniconda3/envs/crewai-venv-3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages/crewai/agent/core.py", line 951, in _get_native_mcp_tools
    raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to get native MCP tools: {e}") from e
RuntimeError: Failed to get native MCP tools: cannot access local variable 'tools_list' where it is not associated with a value
```

### Possible Solution

Remove `transport_on_close` argument when [initializing the client](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/main/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/transports/sse.py#L69)

### Additional context

N/A

linked_prs.title: fix: remove invalid param from sse client
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/transports/sse.py b/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/transports/sse.py
index ce418c51fe..c2184e7d01 100644
--- a/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/transports/sse.py
+++ b/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/transports/sse.py
@@ -66,7 +66,6 @@ async def connect(self) -> Self:
             self._transport_context = sse_client(
                 self.url,
                 headers=self.headers if self.headers else None,
-                terminate_on_close=True,
             )
 
             read, write = await self._transport_context.__aenter__()
diff --git a/lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_sse_transport.py b/lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_sse_transport.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a714c6ce73
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_sse_transport.py
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+"""Tests for SSE transport."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from crewai.mcp.transports.sse import SSETransport
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_sse_transport_connect_does_not_pass_invalid_args():
+    """Test that SSETransport.connect() doesn't pass invalid args to sse_client.
+
+    The sse_client function does not accept terminate_on_close parameter.
+    """
+    transport = SSETransport(
+        url="http://localhost:9999/sse",
+        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer test"},
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(ConnectionError) as exc_info:
+        await transport.connect()
+
+    assert "unexpected keyword argument" not in str(exc_info.value)
\ No newline at end of file
